items.q: A chronic alcoholic presents with acute confusion, bilateral sixth nerve palsies, and ataxia. Administration of intravenous thiamine improves the ophthalmoplegia. What erythrocyte assay confirms thiamine deficiency?
o: Erythrocyte transketolase activity increase upon adding TPP
Erythrocyte glutathione reductase activation by FAD
items.exp: Thiamine deficiency is diagnostically confirmed by measuring erythrocyte transketolase activity before and after adding thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP). An activity increase >15-25% confirms deficiency.
r: Correct. Erythrocyte transketolase activation by TPP is the diagnostic gold standard.
Incorrect. Glutathione reductase activation by FAD tests for riboflavin (B2) deficiency.
Incorrect. Methylmalonic acid tests for vitamin B12 deficiency.
Incorrect. Transaminases test for B6 or liver injury.
items.kp: Erythrocyte transketolase activity stimulated by exogenous thiamine pyrophosphate confirms thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency.

items.q: A patient presenting with pellagra (photosensitive dermatitis, diarrhea, and cognitive dementia) is found to have a diet deficient in niacin. Which amino acid can endogenously synthesize niacin in the liver using vitamin B6 as a cofactor?
items.exp: Approximately 60 mg of dietary tryptophan can be converted into 1 mg of niacin (nicotinic acid). This pathway requires pyridoxal phosphate (B6) and riboflavin (B2); defects in tryptophan absorption (Hartnup disease) also cause pellagra.
r: Correct. Tryptophan is the dietary precursor converted to niacin.
Incorrect. Tyrosine synthesizes catecholamines and melanin.
Incorrect. Phenylalanine is converted to tyrosine.
Incorrect. Methionine enters the SAM cycle.
items.kp: Dietary tryptophan is converted to niacin (vitamin B3) at a 60:1 ratio in a pathway requiring pyridoxal phosphate (B6) as a cofactor.

items.q: Warfarin anticoagulation is monitored via the prothrombin time (INR). Warfarin exerts its therapeutic effect by inhibiting which enzyme required for vitamin K recycling?
items.exp: Warfarin competitively inhibits VKORC1, preventing reduction of vitamin K epoxide back to active hydroquinone. Lacking reduced vitamin K, gamma-glutamyl carboxylase cannot carboxylate clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X.
r: Correct. Warfarin inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase (VKORC1).
Incorrect. Gamma-glutamyl carboxylase uses reduced vitamin K; warfarin inhibits the reductase.
Incorrect. CYP2C9 metabolizes warfarin.
Incorrect. Prothrombinase is the Factor Xa/Va clotting complex.

items.q: A strict vegan of 6 years develops paresthesias in the feet, loss of vibratory sense, spastic gait, and macrocytic anemia. What laboratory finding differentiates vitamin B12 deficiency from folate deficiency?
items.exp: Both B12 and folate deficiencies cause megaloblastic anemia, hypersegmented neutrophils, and elevated homocysteine. However, methylmalonic acid is elevated ONLY in B12 deficiency because B12 is cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase.
r: Correct. Methylmalonic acid is elevated only in B12 deficiency, distinguishing it from folate deficiency.
Incorrect. Homocysteine is elevated in both B12 and folate deficiencies.
Incorrect. Hypersegmented neutrophils occur in both.
Incorrect. Macrocytosis occurs in both.

items.q: Why does administration of high-dose folic acid alone in a patient with undiagnosed vitamin B12 deficiency correct the anemia while permitting irreversible neurological subacute combined degeneration to progress?
o: Folate bypasses the methyl-THF trap to restore thymidylate synthesis for erythropoiesis but cannot rescue B12-dependent methylmalonyl-CoA mutase in myelin
Folic acid directly neurotoxic to dorsal spinal columns
Folic acid inhibits cobalamin uptake in the ileum
Folate accelerates myelin degradation by activating microglia
items.exp: Folate supplies dihydrofolate directly, bypassing the B12-dependent methionine synthase step to rescue thymidylate synthesis and resolve macrocytic anemia. However, methylmalonyl-CoA mutase remains inactive, allowing myelin damage to progress undetected.
r: Correct. Folate bypasses the trap to cure anemia but leaves myelin-damaging B12 deficiency untreated.
Incorrect. Folate is not neurotoxic.
Incorrect. It does not block ileal B12 uptake.
Incorrect. Folate does not activate microglia to destroy myelin.

items.q: An infant born with periorificial and acral vesiculobullous and pustular dermatitis, chronic diarrhea, and alopecia is diagnosed with acrodermatitis enteropathica. Which trace element is deficient due to an intestinal transporter defect?
items.exp: Acrodermatitis enteropathica is an autosomal recessive mutation in SLC39A4 (ZIP4), the intestinal zinc uptake transporter. Zinc deficiency causes periorificial rashes, alopecia, diarrhea, and immune dysfunction.
r: Correct. Zinc deficiency causes acrodermatitis enteropathica.
Incorrect. Copper deficiency causes Menkes disease (kinky hair, arterial aneurysms).
Incorrect. Selenium deficiency causes Keshan cardiomyopathy.
Incorrect. Chromium deficiency causes glucose intolerance.

items.q: Menkes disease is an X-linked recessive disorder of copper metabolism caused by mutations in ATP7A. Defective activity of which copper-dependent enzyme accounts for brittle, sparse, kinky hair ('pili torti') and arterial aneurysms?
items.exp: ATP7A defect impairs copper export from enterocytes into blood. Lacking systemic copper, lysyl oxidase cannot crosslink collagen and elastin, causing tortuous arteries, aneurysms, bone fractures, and pili torti.
r: Correct. Lysyl oxidase requires copper; its inactivity causes connective tissue and vascular defects.
Incorrect. Cytochrome c oxidase defect causes muscle hypotonia.
Incorrect. SOD1 defect causes motor neuron disease.
Incorrect. Tyrosinase failure causes albinism.

items.q: Keshan disease is an endemic juvenile cardiomyopathy described in areas of rural China with low soil content of which trace mineral, an essential component of glutathione peroxidase?
items.exp: Selenium is incorporated as selenocysteine into glutathione peroxidase, an essential antioxidant enzyme protecting myocardium against coxackievirus-induced oxidative injury in Keshan disease.
r: Correct. Selenium deficiency causes Keshan cardiomyopathy.
Incorrect. Molybdenum is required for xanthine oxidase and sulfite oxidase.
Incorrect. Manganese is in mitochondrial SOD2.
Incorrect. Iodine is required for thyroid hormones.

items.q: Which fat-soluble vitamin acts primarily as a chain-breaking lipophilic antioxidant, intercalating into membrane phospholipid bilayers to scavenge peroxyl free radicals and protect polyunsaturated lipids?
items.exp: Vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol) is the principal lipid-soluble antioxidant in cellular membranes, reacting with lipid peroxyl radicals to terminate free radical chain reactions; deficiency causes hemolytic anemia and spinocerebellar ataxia.
r: Correct. Vitamin E is the primary chain-breaking antioxidant protecting membrane lipids.
Incorrect. Vitamin A functions in vision and gene differentiation.
Incorrect. Vitamin D regulates calcium homeostasis.
Incorrect. Vitamin K mediates gamma-carboxylation.

items.q: A patient undergoing long-term total parenteral nutrition without trace element supplementation develops severe glucose intolerance and peripheral neuropathy. Deficiency of which mineral cofactor for chromodulin is responsible?
items.exp: Chromium functions as a cofactor in chromodulin (low-molecular-weight chromium-binding substance), which potentiates insulin receptor tyrosine kinase activity; deficiency causes insulin resistance and hyperglycemia.
r: Correct. Chromium potentiates insulin action; deficiency causes glucose intolerance.
Incorrect. Zinc deficiency causes dermatitis and diarrhea.
Incorrect. Copper deficiency causes microcytic anemia.
Incorrect. Manganese deficiency causes impaired glycosaminoglycan synthesis.
